Arta Card System

A focused extension to Arta's product system for portfolio-secured card applications, decisioning, AI guidance, and partner-brand configuration. Everything on this page is rendered with the system's real generated tokens and component styles — the same CSS that drives the Storybook and the interactive prototype. This page is generated from the system, so it cannot drift from it.

01
Clarity before consent

Fees, risks and the pledge are understood before anything is agreed to. Disclosure prominence is a platform rule, not a style choice.

02
Member control before action

The AI explains and recommends; money never moves and assets are never sold without explicit member confirmation.

03
Brand flexibility within financial guardrails

Partners express their brand freely — the integrity of consequential financial decisions is not configurable.

Token architecture

Three tiers

Naming is a fixed three-part structure — [namespace] · [tier] · [role]. A ref layer of raw ladders (10–90 colour steps, 4px grid); a sys layer of semantic intent that may only alias ref; a cmp layer of per-component contracts where hardcoded values fail the build. A partner theme is a sys-override file with zero component code.

#a8cdf0 → ref.color.sky.40 → sys.action.primary → cmp.btn.primary.bg → .arta-btn

Semantic tokens

Card domain added

Components never reference blue-500 — they reference intent, and intent resolves through the theme. Financial semantics are kept separate from generic semantics: they exist only in the lending domain and are all platform policy 🔒 — a partner may tune lightness for contrast, but the hue family is locked at build time.

Typography & the legal style

Legal style added

Two brand faces, verified from artafinance.com's CSS: Rotunda (self-hosted, thin→black) is the UI and product-display face; Ofelia Display 500 (Adobe Typekit) is the marketing headline face. What lending adds is a legal type style — generous line-height, no letterspacing, footnote support — because disclosure text must be genuinely readable, not merely present. Its size and line-height are compliance-locked minimums.

Recommended limit

Protected pattern

The flagship lending pattern: the limit is computed in the open — eligible value × published advance rates, buffer held back, "why this limit" one tap away. The result, the math, the buffer disclosure and the 7-days'-notice line are platform policy, identical for every brand. Themeable: surfaces, type, radius, accent.

Decision states

Every outcome designed

Every outcome ships a next step — approval is not the only designed state. The status colour, its prominence, and the presence of a next step are platform policy. Presenting pending as approved is structurally impossible.

approvedpendingaction requireddeclined

For a portfolio-secured limit the counter-offer becomes a phased limit — private positions count at their next official NAV, so the limit starts lower and rises automatically. Nothing is declined; the limit follows the assets.

AI interaction

Boundaries are platform policy

One anatomy for every AI moment: Explain → Recommend → Confirm → Act. The AI may observe, explain and recommend freely; moving money, selling assets, changing the repayment source or modifying card settings all require explicit confirmation first. The assistant's name can be white-labelled — its decision boundaries cannot.

Friday's card payment exceeds the cash in your settlement account by S$7,400.

Two T-bill rungs mature within 9 days — covering this at zero cost, without selling positions in a down week.

Uses: statement · settlement balance · portfolio positions. Explained, confirmed, executed, audited. High-impact choices escalate to a named specialist.

White-label configuration

Three kinds of data

Configuration is three kinds of data, not one theme file — brand, product and platform governance each have their own owner and change process. There is no ArtaOfferCard and NorthstarOfferCard: only OfferCard, rendered under a provider. Same data, same hierarchy, same decision logic, same disclosures — only the brand layer changes.

Partners cannot hide or de-emphasise fees, remove the market-movement explanation, alter a decisioning outcome, present pending as approved, drop the next step from a decline, pre-check a consent, let the AI act without confirmation, or hide which data the AI used.
